artifact_types.note: An APPROVED_REPORT because it is an agreement somebody signed, not a measurement of anything.
SYSTEM_OF_RECORD for its own system, what arrived, which is exactly why rank cannot arbitrate between it and the invoice.
SYSTEM_OF_RECORD for its own system, what was billed, which is exactly why rank cannot arbitrate between it and the receipt.

sections.heading: The exception
sections.purpose: State the total variance and the tolerance it broke, in that order. This is the paragraph that decides whether anyone senior reads the rest; it must say plainly that the buyer can no longer clear this.

sections.heading: Where the variance sits
sections.purpose: Split the variance two ways — billed for what did not arrive, and billed at a rate that was not agreed — and say which line each sits on. Do not give the clean line a paragraph; a line that matched warrants a clause.

sections.heading: Status and what is needed
sections.purpose: Where the exception stands and what has to happen for it to move. Written while it is still open, so it asks for a decision rather than reporting one.

sections.heading: The settlement
sections.purpose: What was billed, what the supplier conceded, and what is actually being paid. Lead with the figure being approved, not with the one on the invoice.

sections.heading: Authority for the decision
sections.purpose: Who approved this and under what delegation. State that the variance exceeded the tolerance and that this is therefore Finance's decision — the memo is the record that the approval chain was followed, and a memo that leaves the approver implicit is not that record.

sections.heading: What the close carries
sections.purpose: The accrual posted at close, and — plainly, rather than left to a reader's inference — that it is built from what was received at the contracted rate, not from what was invoiced. This is the sentence that connects a site receipting note to the general ledger.

sections.heading: Still outstanding
sections.purpose: The undelivered balance carried into next month, and that it is a commitment rather than an accrual — nothing has been received, so nothing is owed for it yet. One short paragraph.
sections.note: A "still outstanding" where nothing is. A settlement that closed the order out has no balance to carry, and the memo ends on the approval, which is where a memo about an approval should end. The three sections that make it the record of a decision (settlement, authority, what the close carries) stay required.

sections.heading: The requested change
sections.purpose: What the supplier asked for and why it is being held. State the second approver is outstanding without naming a date it will be resolved by — there is not one.

sections.heading: Counterparty
sections.purpose: Which agreement this supplier is engaged under. One or two sentences; this section exists so the change can be tied to a contract, not to restate the contract.

artifact_types.note: The one document below approved standing, matching the one fact below it: a change nobody has countersigned is a draft, whatever the vendor master screen shows.

A workbook off the order book, the receipting system and the ledger, published at close, the same standing the retail month-end model has and for the same reason: it restates no third party's claim, it reports what three systems of record hold. Its lag is longer than any of the six documents beside it: the position is assembled after the ledger locks, not while the cycle is running.
